author: embirico
text:
Remotion is a video workspace designed for a faster, more connected way of working remotely.
Your teammates and their availability are in a dock on the side of your screen, so you can glance over at a teammate and instantly talk live—instead of typing or scheduling a meeting. https://t.co/pB4zuSqHes

author: embirico
text:
Remote teams are stuck in endless texting and back to back meetings.

They miss the speed and energy of spontaneously talking live—a core part of how teams ideate, help each other, and build relationships

author: embirico
text:
When we started in 2019, many teams viewed remote as a last resort: it’s harder to build a fast-moving, close knit team remotely.

With covid, teams struggled to connect: Emails initially went up 20%. Now they want to more talk more often, but avg mtg length is still 48 mins.

author: embirico
text:
My cofounder @potatoearecool and I met in college and came together around a shared belief and mission.
Belief: People thrive when they can live and work on their own terms.
Mission: Help more teams embrace remote work. https://t.co/KWiKYa3Wig

author: embirico
text:
Remote work shouldn’t feel remote. Excited to share how @remotionco helps remote teams move faster and feel connected.

@jornvandijk The different decisions play off each other in nuanced ways. For example Paper is great for collaborative, high trust teams, but falls short with maintaining top-down structure. Notion is better at helping someone central organize the team's content.
(I used to be a PM on Paper.)

author: embirico
text: @jornvandijk Teams that "want to be friends" will use social tools like Donut, icebreakers, or in general tools with more emojis 🙂

author: embirico
text: @jornvandijk Lower trust teams need more supervision tools. At the extreme you have Upwork's "Worker Diary" which is a screen capture tool: https://t.co/sYCzqa9HhI

author: embirico
text:
@jornvandijk Writing-first teams tend to use long-form tools like email/Notion/Paper.

Video-first teams either have more video calls or use tools like Loom to record video.

author: embirico
text:
@jornvandijk More consensus-driven teams need a high meeting load or put decision making in structured tools like Jira; maybe GDocs / Paper.

More decentralized teams have decisions made locally. Maybe documented in PRs, Figma, etc. FYI'd in Slack/Email.

author: embirico
embirico
text:
@jornvandijk I’d start by thinking about what kind of remote culture the team wants, then find tools to fill gaps.

Example choices:
- async vs face-to-face
- include everyone on decisions vs decentralized autonomy
- writing first vs video first
- high/low trust
- friends or just colleagues

author: embirico
text:
@Marc_Low @jmj Zoom: Scheduled meetings.
Slack: Text messaging.

-> Important things only are discussed over transactional video calls, the rest is text.
Text is great for broadcast but is less personal, more prone to misinterpretation, and leads to fewer sparks of insight or energy.
